We can progrommatically access the properties of the materials like this:


```{python}
import molecularnodes as mn
from molecularnodes.nodes import geometry as g
from nodebpy import shader as s

cv = mn.Canvas(engine="EEVEE", resolution=(800, 800), transparent=True)
```


```{python}
# | label: fig-material-example
# | fig-cap: A simple Ambient Occlusion material that is performant and aesthetically pleasing. Material properties can be changed through the material interface.
# | layout-ncol: 2
# | fig-subcap:
# |   - "distance=2.0, samples=128"
# |   - "distance=0.15, samples=128"

with s.material("Custom Material") as mat:
    mat.nodes.clear()
    col = mn.nodes.shader.MNColor()
    ao = s.AmbientOcclusion(col, distance=2.0, samples=128)
    ao.o.color >> s.MaterialOutput().i.surface

mol = mn.Molecule.fetch("8H1B").add_style("surface", material=mat)

cv.frame_object(mol)
cv.snapshot()

ao.i.distance.default_value = 0.15
cv.snapshot()
```


```{python}
# | label: fig-change-material-flat
# | layout-ncol: 1
# | fig-subcap:
# |   - "Reduced AO distance detection"
# |   - "Flat Outline material"
mol.tree.tree.nodes["Style Surface"].inputs["Material"].default_value = mn.material.append_material("MN Flat")
cv.snapshot()

# mol.styles[0].material.math_value = 0.1
# cv.snapshot()
```

Propeties for the material interface are based on the inputs of the nodes in the material.


## Render Engines and Materials

The different render engines handle materials diferently.
```{python}
import MDAnalysis as mda
import itertools
from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import PSF, DCD

cv = mn.Canvas(resolution=(800, 800), transparent=True)
```


```{python}
# | warning: false
# | label: fig-eevee-raytracing
# | fig-cap: "How different materials behave in each render engine"
# | layout-ncol: 2
# | fig-subcap:
# |   - "Cycles + Default"
# |   - "EEVEE + Default"
# |   - "Cycles + Ambient Occlusion"
# |   - "EEVEE + Ambient Occlusion"
# |   - "Cycles + Flat Outline"
# |   - "EEVEE + Flat Outline"
# |   - "Cycles + Squishy"
# |   - "EEVEE + Squishy"

mol = mn.Molecule.load(PSF, DCD)
with mol.tree.reset() as (atoms, join):
    style = g.StyleSpheres(sphere_geometry="Instance")
    style.i["Quality"].default_value = 4
    color = g.ColorElement(c=g.RandomColor(g.ChainID()))
    atoms >> g.SetColor(color=color) >> style >> join

cv.frame_view(mol)
engines = [mn.scene.Cycles(samples=32), mn.scene.EEVEE()]
materials = [
    "MN Default",
    "MN Ambient Occlusion",
    "MN Flat",
    "MN Squishy",
]
for mat, eng in itertools.product(materials, engines):
    cv.engine = eng
    style.i.material.default_value = mn.material.append_material(mat)
    cv.snapshot()
```
